purpose: Presents an optional program: NAD+ therapy by video call, as an injection or a form taken under the tongue, prescribed by a clinician and shipped to the patient's door. It exists for practices that offer longevity care alongside joint care, and it can be switched off for those that do not.
owner_notes: NAD+ is an optional program. If a practice does not offer it, it is switched off, and the page, its line in the Treatments menu, its card on All treatments and every mention of it across the site go together.

This page is about prescription care by video call, not treatment at home. Its small print is different from the other Treatments pages: it is about compounded medications, and there is no California stem cell notice here.

The three program cards are samples and show no price. Book a Consultation, Request this program and Talk to a provider all open the Booking page, and See Programs at the top only moves down the page; nothing is sold or paid for here.

The page speaks about energy, the brain and nerves, and ageing in the practice's name, and says what is not known. Ava says what the page explains and keeps to its own honest line: it differs from person to person, and some people notice little change.
The vial is pictured three times, at the top, in Programs and in Delivery Options, and each picture carries a Sample picture stamp on this example.
replace: Programs: the three sample program cards are replaced by your own programs and prices.
The closing band, Talk to a Provider: your phone number replaces the sample {{site.phone}}.
The vial pictures are stand-ins, each stamped Sample picture; they do not show your products.
The header and footer carry your practice name in place of the sample name {{site.name}}.
keep: The small print at the bottom: compounded medications are not FDA-approved drugs, a medical evaluation is required, individual results vary, and some uses may be considered off-label.
The answer to How long does NAD+ therapy take to work: it differs from person to person, some people notice little change, and the clinician adjusts or stops the plan.
The safety answer: side effects are possible with any treatment, compounded NAD+ is not FDA-approved, and results vary.
The line under Why NAD+ that whether raising levels changes how a person feels is still being studied.
Consult required on the program cards: a licensed clinician reviews each patient before anything is prescribed.

top.say: The top of the page introduces NAD plus therapy, as an injection or a form taken under the tongue, with two buttons, Book a Consultation and See Programs. The vial pictured there is stamped Sample picture.

why-nad.say: Why NAD plus gives the page's explanation of what NAD plus does in the body, and what is not known, such as whether raising levels changes how a person feels. Its chart is labelled illustrative.

programs.say: Programs shows three sample program cards with no price on them, which is where a practice lists its own programs and prices.

delivery-options.say: Delivery Options compares the two forms side by side: an injection, or a form absorbed under the tongue.

faq.say: The questions at the bottom cover what NAD plus therapy is, how the two forms differ and how long it takes, with the honest answer that some people notice little change.

talk-to-a-provider.say: Talk to a Provider is the closing band, with one button that opens the Booking page and the phone number beside it.

questions.q: What is the NAD plus page for?
alt: What's the NAD+ and longevity page?
Why is there an NAD page?
What does the NAD+ page do?
questions.say: It presents an optional program: NAD plus therapy by video call, as an injection or a form taken under the tongue, shipped to the patient's door. The page explains what NAD plus is, shows sample programs and compares the two forms. It only belongs on your site if your practice offers this.

questions.q: Can I take NAD plus off my site?
alt: Can I take NAD+ off, or add hormones or peptides?
What if I don't offer NAD?
Is the NAD+ page optional?
questions.say: Yes. NAD plus is an optional program. When it is switched off, the page, its line in the Treatments menu and every mention of it go together. Hormone and peptide pages also exist, switched off on this example. As for whether they are in your package, I don't have that. Your contact for the website can tell you.

questions.q: Where are the NAD plus programs and prices?
alt: Is there a price on the NAD+ page?
Where do my NAD prices go?
Where are the NAD+ programs?
questions.say: In the part called Programs, a little way down the NAD plus page. On this example the three cards are samples and show no figure, only the words Pricing on consultation or Consult required. A practice lists its own programs and prices there.

questions.q: What do I change on the NAD plus page?
alt: What do I replace on the NAD+ page?
What on the NAD page is a sample?
Why does the vial say Sample picture?
questions.say: Mainly the three program cards, which are samples: you list your own programs and prices. Your phone number replaces the sample {{site.phone}} at the bottom. The vial pictures are stand-ins too. Each is stamped Sample picture, and they do not show your products.

questions.q: What has to stay on the NAD plus page?
alt: What is the small print on the NAD+ page?
What can't come off the NAD page?
questions.say: The small print at the bottom. It says compounded medications are not FDA-approved drugs, that a medical evaluation is required, and that individual results vary. The answer saying some people notice little change stays too.

questions.q: How does a patient start NAD plus from this page?
alt: Can patients buy NAD+ on the website?
What do the buttons on the NAD page do?
questions.say: Book a Consultation, Request this program and Talk to a provider all open the Booking page. Nothing is sold or paid for on the page. A licensed clinician reviews the patient's case first and recommends a form based on their labs and goals.

questions.q: How long does NAD plus take to work?
alt: How long does NAD+ therapy take to work?
When will I feel a difference?
questions.say: The page says it differs from person to person, and some people notice little change. Your clinician checks how you are doing at each follow-up and adjusts or stops the plan. Individual results vary.

questions.q: What's the difference between the injection and the one under the tongue?
alt: Injection or sublingual, which is right for me?
Do I have to use needles?
questions.say: The page says both are prescribed by a clinician by video call. The injection goes under the skin or into muscle and is shipped to your door. The other form is absorbed under the tongue, with no needles. Your clinician recommends one based on your goals and labs.
